conviction_note: Seven small, mostly proxy or contract-level findings net to a slight positive (+1.7 impact_sum), driven mainly by a short position equal to about 52% of shares outstanding that rose for four straight settlements and by power-semi peers (ST, onsemi) guiding up after Wolfspeed last spoke. The scaled number is far smaller (p_up 52 x abs 14.5 = +0.58) because the stock has sold 3 of its last 4 prints, the evidence is mostly proxy, and nothing found is a company-level number that decides the Q1 print or the first Q2 guide. The gap between the two numbers is the reaction history overruling weak positive proxies.
bar: Company guide for fiscal Q1 2027: revenue $140-160M (midpoint $150M), non-GAAP gross margin negative, non-GAAP opex $62-66M (8-K ex.99.1, 2026-08-19, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000895419/000089541926000049/ex991q4-26.htm). Consensus revenue $150.0M (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/WOLF/earnings-forecasts) and $153.2M (FXEmpire, https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/wolf/earnings); non-GAAP EPS consensus -$2.02 on both, -$1.76 on TipRanks from 2 analysts (https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/DE:CR6/earnings). Revenue bar is sourced to a company guide with two agreeing estimate sources; the EPS bar is disputed (-2.02 vs -1.76). The real bar tonight is the first fiscal Q2 2027 revenue guide, for which no consensus was found.
positioning_check: Short interest 27,376,417 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement = 51.7% of 52.99M shares outstanding (as of 2026-08-13, S-3ASR), days to cover 4.25; up from 24.64M (08-31), 26.10M (09-15), 26.85M (09-30, DTC 11.4) (https://equibles.com/stocks/wolf/short-interest, read 2026-11-04; massive.com quote page confirms 27.38M / 4.3 days as of 2026-10-15). Part of it is very probably convert-arbitrage hedging: the selling-stockholder table of the 2026-09-16 S-3ASR is dominated by convertible-note funds (LMR, Whitebox, Sculptor, HBK, CSS, Slate Path) and Renesas holds 2L converts, so the 'crowded short' is partly hedge, not all directional. Skew: 25d put minus call IV = -5.88 vol points, i.e. upside paid; put/call OI 0.86. Run-up -19.35% 5d, -31.51% 20d, -70.8% from 52w high; spot $21.49 sits just below the $23.33 average analyst target (MarketBeat, 1 Buy / 3 Hold / 1 Sell).

findings.finding: Short interest is 27.4M shares, 51.7% of the 53.0M shares outstanding, at the 2026-10-15 settlement (days to cover 4.25), and it has risen at every settlement since August (24.6M on 08-31, 26.1M on 09-15, 26.9M on 09-30); with the stock -31.5% over 20 days into a print where the option market already pays more for calls than puts (skew -5.9 vol points), a release that is merely in line removes the reason for the short and a squeeze is a mechanism of its own.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No squeeze reaction in the four post-emergence prints in the baseline: -18.2% (2025-10-29), -9.7% (2026-02-04), +17.6% (2026-05-05), -9.4% (2026-08-19); the one up move came with a short interest of a similar order (Schaeffer's flagged WOLF as a squeeze candidate on 2026-05-13).
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public, but the skew shows only part of it: if the market treated the short as a squeeze setup the call wing would be bid well beyond -5.9 points and the stock would not have fallen 19% in the five sessions before the print. Much of the short is convert-arb hedging (see positioning_check), which caps how much of it is forced to cover, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: massive.com quote page, 27.38M shares short, 4.3 days to cover as of 2026-10-15 (https://massive.com/quote/wolf); Tickeron, about 51.8% of the public float short (https://tickeron.com/blogs/wolfspeed-wolf-drops-19-6-in-30-days-despite-1-5-billion-financing-news-24294/). Same FINRA data underneath, so not independent evidence.

findings.finding: Power-semiconductor peers that reported after Wolfspeed last spoke (2026-08-19) guided up: STMicro (2026-10-29) printed Q3 revenue +17.9% y/y, Power and Discrete +11.3% y/y, and guided Q4 to $4.15B, +10.5% sequential and +24.7% y/y; onsemi (2026-11-02) printed Q3 revenue +11% y/y ($1.722B) and guided Q4 to $1.715-1.815B, citing accelerating AI data-center and industrial power demand. Wolfspeed's own Q1 guide ($140-160M) is flat on Q4's $149.6M, so a peer-consistent Q2 guide would sit above flat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide has driven every recent reaction: 2026-08-19 flat Q1 guide (midpoint at consensus) -9.4%; 2025-10-29 weak outlook -18.2%; 2026-05-05 +17.6%. The name has not paid for an in-line guide.
findings.why_not_priced: WOLF fell 19% in the five sessions after ST's report and through onsemi's, so the stock has not traded with its peers' guides; if this were priced the stock would not be at a fresh 20-day low into the print. It is a proxy: neither peer quantified silicon carbide or automotive SiC, and Wolfspeed's own call said auto mix is unpredictable, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: onsemi Q3 2026 8-K ex.99.1, 2026-11-02 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001097864/000114036126041580/ef20084671_ex99-1.htm) - a different company and document from ST's release. Neither one isolates SiC.

findings.finding: Two named supply contracts were announced after the Q4 call: Infineon moves its long-term Wolfspeed SiC substrate supply from 150mm to 200mm wafers in a new multi-year agreement (2026-10-15), and BorgWarner signed a multi-year supply deal for Wolfspeed 1200V SiC devices on its next 800V inverter platform (2026-10-29). Materials revenue was the weak line in Q4 ($43.3M against $78.4M a year earlier, with customers in the 150-to-200mm transition), so the Infineon move lands on that line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline print was decided by a contract announcement; the Q4 release's partnership news (LITEON, Toyota OBC, a European Tier 1 award) did not stop a -9.4% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Neither contract carries a value or volume, so no estimate can include it; management can quantify either tonight in the Q2 guide or materials commentary. The stock fell after both announcements, which is what it looks like when the contracts are not in the price. Small, because the timing of revenue is multi-year and undisclosed.
findings.independence: BorgWarner deal: https://evertiq.com/design/2026-10-30-wolfspeed-announces-sic-device-supply-deal-with-borgwarner (a different counterparty and document). Q4 materials figures: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000895419/000089541926000049/ex991q4-26.htm.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-07 Wolfspeed announced a conditional Department of War (Office of Strategic Capital) commitment for up to $1.5B: a senior secured, 30-year delayed-draw term loan at Treasury plus a provisional 1.25-1.75%, with interest capitalisable for five years and the first $600M refinancing the secured notes due 2030, in exchange for warrants up to 7.5% of fully diluted equity and a $750M minimum contribution that may include equity or excess cash. The call is the first chance to update definitive-agreement progress and say how the $750M will be met; the company held $1.09B of cash at 2026-06-28.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose about 6% on the announcement (TIKR) and then gave it all back and more by 2026-10-30 on dilution worry (Tickeron). No earlier print turned on financing in the post-emergence history.
findings.why_not_priced: What the money buys is a cheaper, longer refinance of the 2030 secured notes plus capex for GaN/SiC/rad-hard programmes, not a demand ramp (revenue guide is flat), so per lesson 4 it is neither distress nor growth. The open question is the $750M contribution: if management says it can be met from existing cash, the dilution discount the stock took after 2026-10-07 unwinds; if it signals an equity raise, it deepens. The press release does not say which, which is why the range is wide and the point is near zero.
findings.independence: Runtimewire on the 8-K terms ($750M minimum contribution including equity or excess cash; first $600M refinances 2030 notes): https://runtimewire.com/article/wolfspeed-conditional-defense-loan-refinance-2030-notes. Tickeron, 2026-10-30, on the give-back and dilution concern: https://tickeron.com/blogs/wolfspeed-wolf-drops-19-6-in-30-days-despite-1-5-billion-financing-news-24294/.

findings.finding: The Q4 FY26 operating cash flow of -$54M included a $41M benefit from lower inventory, so the underlying burn was about -$95M a quarter with non-GAAP gross margin at -20% and management putting gross-margin breakeven near an $800M annual revenue run rate, against a guided ~$600M run rate; Q1 guides gross margin still negative, so a repeat inventory release is unlikely to flatter Q1 cash flow.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin and cash were cited in the 2026-08-19 sell-off (-9.4%) and the 2026-02-04 one (-9.7%); the stock sells negative gross margin prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The headline OCF (-$54M) is what screens and previews carry; the $41M inventory benefit sits in the call commentary. If the market priced the -$95M underlying run rate, the conditional loan's equity contribution would not be the open question it is. Largely inside what the company already guided (negative GM), and the crowded short shrinks a negative, so it is small.
findings.independence: Q4 8-K ex.99.1 confirms OCF -$54.1M, FCF -$60.9M, non-GAAP GM -20%, cash $1,088.6M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000895419/000089541926000049/ex991q4-26.htm). The inventory figure itself rests on the TradingKey/Mitrade summary of the call.

findings.finding: Reports at the Q4 print said the broad rollout of 800V DC data-center power architecture is delayed beyond 2028, which pushes out the timing of revenue from Wolfspeed's 800V products, the segment management presented as its growth line (AI data-center revenue +20% sequential in Q4).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raised in the August coverage of the -9.4% reaction; no separate reaction on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it was public at the last print. It remains filed because the Q2 guide and AI data-center commentary tonight will show whether the delay has hit near-term data-center orders; the source is an AI-generated summary, so it is sized near zero.
findings.independence: onsemi (2026-11-02) cites accelerating AI data-center power demand, which points the other way for near-term demand: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001097864/000114036126041580/ef20084671_ex99-1.htm

findings.finding: Digitimes reported on 2026-09-03 that Chinese 6-inch SiC substrate supply is tightening and prices are expected to rise, after an oversupply price war took large-order channel prices to about $200-300 a wafer by late Q2 2026. That would ease the price pressure on Wolfspeed's materials business, which fell 45% y/y in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Materials weakness was part of the 2026-08-19 -9.4% reaction; there is no history of this line being a positive surprise.
findings.source_date: 2026-09-03 (from URL path; headline and metadata only, body paywalled, snippet_only)
findings.why_not_priced: Paywalled trade press that the US coverage does not cite. It is a narrow proxy: 6-inch Chinese pricing, while Wolfspeed sells mostly 200mm substrates into a customer transition. So it is sized minimal.
findings.independence: Digitimes Chinese-language piece (date not confirmed from URL) on Chinese 6-inch prices bottoming and recovering: https://www.digitimes.com.tw/tech/dt/n/shwnws.asp?id=761681 - same publisher, so not independent.

outside_window.finding: Definitive agreements, the first $600M tranche and warrant issuance under the Department of War conditional loan have no date; whatever is not updated on the call resolves after the window.

baseline_tension: The slight positive lean agrees with the skew (upside paid, -5.9) and with the crowded short, and cuts against the reaction history (3 of 4 prints sold) and the -31.5% 20-day slide; p_up is held near 50 because none of the findings is a company number that decides the print.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sells prints, 3 of 4 down): peer-guide finding 0.8 -> 0.6 and contracts finding 0.5 -> 0.4; p_up 53 -> 52.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the DoW loan buys a refinance and capex, not a demand ramp, and the $750M contribution route is open; 0.5 -> 0.3 with a wide symmetric band.
Lesson 7 (a crowded short shrinks a negative): cash-burn finding -0.8 -> -0.6; the positioning finding stays at +1.0.
Lesson 5 (a narrow proxy is sized small): Digitimes 6-inch pricing 0.3 -> 0.2; 800V delay finding, already public at the last print, -0.3 -> -0.2.
Lesson 8 and the core (a first Q2 guide, thin 5-analyst coverage, sizes understated historically): abs_move_pct 14.0 -> 14.5, above the 11.75 event-implied and near the 13.66 median.
